sections.title: David Becomes King of Israel
observations: After the death of Saul, David is anointed king over Judah, and later, all of Israel. This marks a significant transition in Israel's leadership and the fulfillment of God's promise to David.
David's kingship is established in Hebron, where he reigns for seven and a half years before moving to Jerusalem, which becomes the political and spiritual center of Israel.

sections.title: The Capture of Jerusalem
observations: David's conquest of Jerusalem from the Jebusites demonstrates his military prowess and strategic thinking. Jerusalem, a city not previously conquered, becomes the new capital of Israel.
The capture of Jerusalem symbolizes God's favor and the establishment of a central place for worship and governance.

sections.title: David's Growing Power and Influence
observations: David's reign is characterized by military victories and the expansion of Israel's territory. His leadership unites the tribes and strengthens the nation.
The chapter highlights the importance of divine guidance in David's decisions, as he seeks the Lord's counsel before engaging in battles.

sections.title: David's Family and Legacy
observations: David's marriages and children are mentioned, reflecting the customs of the time and the importance of lineage in establishing a dynasty.
This section foreshadows future challenges within David's family, which will have significant implications for his reign.

importantVerses.commentary: The tribes of Israel come to David, acknowledging him as their leader, which signifies the unity of the nation under his rule.
David becomes greater and greater, for the Lord, the God of hosts, was with him. This emphasizes the divine support behind David's success.
David inquired of the Lord, and the Lord answered him, showing the importance of seeking God's guidance in leadership decisions.
